questions.q: Why does the game use random.uniform(2, 5) for the delay before the LED lights?
choices: To make the program run faster
To pick an unpredictable decimal delay so the player cannot anticipate the light
To limit the current flowing to the LED
Because the LED needs at least 2 seconds to warm up
questions.explain: random.uniform(2, 5) returns a random decimal between 2 and 5 seconds, with every value equally likely. The unpredictability stops the player from counting and pressing too early.

questions.q: How does the program measure your reaction time using the time module?
choices: It counts how many times the while loop runs
It reads time.time() when the LED lights and again when you press, then subtracts and multiplies by 1000
It uses random.uniform to estimate the time
It asks the GPU for a frame counter
questions.explain: time.time() gives the current moment in seconds. Recording it at the light (start) and at the press (end), then computing (end - start) * 1000, gives the reaction time in milliseconds.

questions.q: With gpiozero's default Button, where does the button's other leg connect, and why is no external resistor needed?
choices: To 5 V, because the Pi runs from a 5 V supply
To GND, because the default pull_up=True uses the Pi's internal pull-up resistor
To another GPIO pin, which acts as the resistor
To 3.3 V through a 330 Ω resistor you must add
questions.explain: Button defaults to pull_up=True, holding the pin HIGH via the Pi's internal pull-up. You wire the other leg to GND so pressing pulls the pin LOW. No external resistor is required for the button.

questions.q: What is switch bounce, and how does bounce_time fix it?
choices: The LED flickering; bounce_time dims it
The button's contacts rapidly make and break on one press, looking like several presses; bounce_time ignores changes for a short window
The Pi rebooting when a button is pressed; bounce_time delays the reboot
Static electricity damaging the pin; bounce_time grounds it
questions.explain: When a switch closes, its metal contacts bounce, producing several rapid edges that the Pi may read as multiple presses. Setting bounce_time (e.g. 0.05 s) tells gpiozero to ignore further changes for that window, so one press counts once.

questions.q: In the score check 'if best is None or reaction_ms < best:', why include 'best is None'?
choices: To make the LED brighter on the first round
Because on the very first round there is no best yet, so any score should be recorded as the best
To convert the time into milliseconds
To stop the while loop after one round
questions.explain: best starts as None (no score recorded). 'best is None' is true on the first round, so the first time is stored as the best; after that, 'reaction_ms < best' records any faster time. This is a conditional handling the empty starting state.
